calibration_anchor.closest_anchor: AI-buzzword product launch with no proof or data
calibration_anchor.why_not_higher: The fact that 'AI agents' is a hot category is not a substitute for proof, data, or a real journalism hook
calibration_anchor.why_not_lower: The product has a reasonable category, but all hype with no evidence

beat_relevance.rationale: AI/enterprise beat exists but pitch is generic category cheerleading

timeliness.rationale: No external hook, news event, or dated moment—only launch

magnitude.rationale: Unknown seed startup, no disclosed user base or revenue

proof_points.rationale: No data, customer, exclusive access, or methodology provided

narrative_quality.rationale: Framing ('future of human-AI collaboration is here') is generic thought leadership

source_credibility.rationale: Unknown startup founders with no background or standing

improvement_suggestions: Replace generic framing with a specific use case or customer story
Bring concrete data: user count, adoption curve, or retention metrics
Tie the pitch to a narrower beat (e.g., workflow automation or particular industry) with named customer proof
evidence_gaps: Actual adoption metrics or traction data
Real-world use case beyond the product description
honest_assessment: This is an AI category talking point, not a story. The angle ('AI agents are the future') is a generic narrative without proof. Journalists will not cover a product for being in a hot category.

next_move.rationale: Hold until there is a real customer or usage story
